A 3D printer prints its material on a heat bed. This heat bed is made of aluminium and should be kept at a constant temperature that matches the melting temperature of the printing material. In this exercises lets say we have polylactic acid and the heat bed temperture needs to be a 60 degrees in the middle of the heat bed. The dimensions of the heat bed is 20 x 20 cm and with a thickness of 0.3 cm. It is heated at all four edges such that the temperature is 100 degrees at the edges. Heat is lost from the heat bed surface on only one side. Make a 2D model in python and predict how long time it takes to reach 60 degrees in the middle of the heat bed assuming that the heat bed to start with is the same temperature as the room air (20 deg C). A plot of the heat bed center temperature over time should be good enough for solving this exercise.    

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import matplotlib.animation as animation

# ----------------------
# Parameters
# ----------------------
Lx = 0.20  # m
Ly = Lx
dx = 0.005
dy = dx
x_grid = np.arange(0, Lx + dx, dx)
y_grid = x_grid

T_air = 20      # ambient temperature
k = 205         # W/m/K
ro = 2700       # kg/m3
cp = 900        # J/kg/K
alpha = k / (ro * cp)  # thermal diffusivity

h = 1         # W/m2/K convection top/bottom
depth = 0.003   # plate thickness
temp_S = 100     # fixed side temperature

Nx = len(x_grid)
Ny = len(y_grid)

# ----------------------
# Initial condition
# ----------------------
T0 = np.full((Nx, Ny), T_air)
T0[:, 0] = temp_S    # left edge
T0[:, -1] = temp_S   # right edge
T0[0, :] = temp_S    # lower edge
T0[-1, :] = temp_S   # upper edge

T0_flat = T0.flatten(order='F')

# ----------------------
# ODE function
# ----------------------
def rates(t, T_flat, k, h, alpha, T_air, dx, dy, depth, Nx, Ny, temp_S):
    
    T = T_flat.reshape((Nx, Ny), order = 'F') # reshape the 1D state variable input to 2D for better intuitive understanding
    dTdt = np.zeros_like(T) # make a 0 2D array of the derivatives, with same shape as state variable (temperature)

    m_cell = dx * dy * depth * ro # calculate the mass of a single cell 
    A_surface = dx * dy # calculate the surface area of a single cell (from which we loss heat)

    # Interior nodes
    for i in range(1, Nx-1): # loop over the x dimension in the outoer loop
        for j in range(1, Ny-1): # loop over the y dimension in the inner loop
            d2x = (T[i-1,j] - 2*T[i,j] + T[i+1,j]) / dx**2 # conduction in x direction
            d2y = (T[i,j-1] - 2*T[i,j] + T[i,j+1]) / dy**2 # conduction in y direction
            Q_loss = h * (T[i,j] - T_air) * A_surface # energy loss from each cell through the surface  
            dTdt[i,j] = alpha * (d2x + d2y) - Q_loss/ (m_cell * cp) # combine everything in the governing equation

    # Left and right edges (Dirichlet fixed T, by setting the change to 0)
    dTdt[:, 0] = 0
    dTdt[:, -1] = 0
    # upper and lower eges (Dirichlet fixed T, by setting the change to 0)
    dTdt[0, :] = 0
    dTdt[-1, :] = 0

    # ----------------------
    # Flatten to 1D so solve_ivp() can handle the input
    # ----------------------
    return dTdt.flatten(order='F')

# ----------------------
# Solve ODE
# ----------------------
tmax = 500  # seconds
t_eval = np.linspace(0, tmax, 1000)

sol = solve_ivp(
    rates,
    t_span=[0, tmax],
    y0=T0_flat,
    method='BDF',
    t_eval=t_eval,
    args=(k, h, alpha, T_air, dx, dy, depth, Nx, Ny, temp_S)
)


# Animation code below which was with help from ChatGPT
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
vmin, vmax = sol.y.min(), sol.y.max()
pcm = ax.imshow(sol.y[:,0].reshape((Nx, Ny), order='F'),
                vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax,
                origin='lower', extent=[0,Lx,0,Ly],
                aspect='equal', cmap='hot')

cbar = fig.colorbar(pcm, ax=ax)
cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.ScalarFormatter())
cbar.ax.yaxis.get_offset_text().set_visible(False)

ax.plot(Lx/2, Ly/2, 'bo', label='Center')
ax.set_xlabel('x [m]')
ax.set_ylabel('y [m]')
ax.legend()

def update(frame):
    T_frame = sol.y[:, frame].reshape((Nx, Ny), order='F')
    pcm.set_data(T_frame)
    ax.set_title(f"Time: {sol.t[frame]:.1f} s")
    return [pcm]

#ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=len(sol.t), interval=500, blit=True)
ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=len(sol.t), interval=500, blit=False)
plt.show()


# 2D animation is nice to look at, but we want to know the temperature in the middle
# We find all the center positions 
center_idx = (Nx//2) + (Ny//2)*Nx
T_center = sol.y[center_idx, :]

plt.figure()
plt.plot(sol.t, T_center)
plt.xlabel('Time [s]')
plt.ylabel('Center Temperature [°C]')
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

```
